newsitem.title: USA: TV AZTECA IPO PRICE RANGE HIKED UP.
newsitem.headline: TV AZTECA IPO PRICE RANGE HIKED UP.

text.p: Bear Stearns & Co said it will cost more to buy shares in the heated initial public offering of TV Azteca, Mexico's second largest television broadcaster.
The underwriter bumped up the estimated price of shares to between $17 and $19, up from earlier estimates of $15 to $17, an indicator of strong demand.

The number of American Depositary Shares (ADSs) remains 34.0 million globally, bringing total proceeds to roughly $612 million. Azteca has said it plans to use the cash to "provide liquidity to certain minority shareholders" and for general corporate purposes.

The shares will trade on exchanges in New York and Mexico in what is being billed as the second largest IPO by a Mexican firm since the 1994-1995 peso crisis. The IPO is due to price on Thursday for trading on Friday, the underwriter said.

Since its privatization in 1993, TV Azteca has been slowly creeping closer to challenge big-fish Grupo Televisa, which has dominated broadcasting for years in Mexico due to its close ties to Mexico's ruling party. Azteca's weekday audience share during prime time jumped to 37 percent at the end of 1996 from 18 percent in January.
Azteca broadcasts soap operas and news casts -- its most successful hourlong program is a U.S.-style news tabloid show called "Ciudad Desnuda" ("Naked City").
